papers.title: Predicting Rates of Cognitive Decline in Older Adults with Brain- and Cardiac-Imputed Transcripts.
papers.abstract: Severe cognitive decline due to dementia is an important clinical indicator signaling neurodegeneration. Predicting cognitive decline rates can be useful in establishing prognosis and modifying treatment regimens. The rate of decline is highly variable across patients with dementia and may be determined by an interplay of many factors. This variability poses challenges to existing tools for predicting disease progression. Changes in heart and brain tissue have been associated with cognitive decline, yet tissue-specific molecular data are difficult to obtain. In this study, we sought to estimat
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study uses imputed gene expression data from brain and heart tissue to predict the rate of cognitive decline in older adults. The authors leverage tissue-specific molecular profiles, which are otherwise difficult to obtain, to improve prognosis and potentially guide treatment decisions. The approach highlights the value of cross-tissue transcriptomic imputation for modeling complex neurodegenerative outcomes.

papers.title: PCA-mapping and machine learning identify multiple chemotypes with antiplasmodial, β-haematin and haemozoin formation inhibition activity.
papers.abstract: Inhibiting the formation of haemozoin remains a robust, non-genomic target for antiplasmodial drug discovery. While current efforts focus on multistage active compounds that are not pure haemozoin formation inhibitors, this class offers advantages including selectivity for Plasmodium and is associated with lowered resistance risks. With a view to developing cost-effective tools to streamline the discovery process, we developed a high-throughput virtual screening (HTVS) workflow integrating both ligand- and structure-based techniques. Here, we employed a principal component analysis (PCA) enric
papers.summary: This study develops a high-throughput virtual screening workflow that combines ligand- and structure-based methods, including PCA-based mapping and machine learning, to identify compounds that inhibit haemozoin formation in Plasmodium parasites. The approach uncovered multiple chemotypes with antiplasmodial activity, offering a cost-effective strategy for antimalarial drug discovery targeting this non-genomic pathway.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study investigates how the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs affects their ability to disrupt membranes, revealing that tail length is a key determinant of membrane activity. The findings suggest that carmofur and its analogs may act through noncanonical mechanisms beyond their known targets, such as acid ceramidase inhibition or SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibition. This provides insight into the drug's polypharmacology and could inform the design of improved analogs.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Immune Dysregulation and Candidate Drug Targets in Endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory disorder affecting 5-10% of women of reproductive age and is associated with chronic pain and infertility. While research has mainly focused on local lesions, systemic immune dysfunction is increasingly implicated in disease pathogenesis. This study employs single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from women with endometriosis and unaffected controls, combined with integrative analysis of publicly available datasets of menstrual blood and endometrial tissues, to uncover immune dysregulation and therapeutic targ
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from women with endometriosis and controls, combined with public datasets from menstrual blood and endometrial tissue, to characterize systemic immune dysregulation. The analysis identifies altered immune cell populations and candidate drug targets, suggesting that endometriosis involves broader immune system changes beyond local lesions.

papers.title: Benzamides of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles as Anticancer Scaffolds: Synthesis, In Silico and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Indoles and benzimidazoles are important nitrogen-containing heterocyclic scaffolds and are a cornerstone of synthetic drugs. In this study, benzamides of 2-aminophenylindoles and 2-aminophenylbenzimidazoles were synthesized and evaluated for their potential. Further, they were also subjected to computational studies for their ADMET profiling and binding with target proteins. Methods: The synthesized compounds were characterized by ATR-FTIR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR and electrospray ionization mass spectroscopy (ESI-MS). They were screened for their in vitro antibacterial activit
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of benzamide derivatives of 2-(aminophenyl)benzimidazoles and 2-(aminophenyl)indoles and evaluated them for anticancer potential. The compounds were characterized spectroscopically, tested in vitro for antibacterial activity, and subjected to in silico ADMET profiling and molecular docking against target proteins. The work identifies these scaffolds as promising starting points for further anticancer drug development.

papers.title: Virtual Screening and Molecular Dynamics Simulations Identifying Natural Product-Derived Cathepsin K Inhibitors as Potential Therapeutics for Osteoporosis.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis is a prevalent skeletal disorder characterized by excessive bone resorption and an increased risk of fragility fracture. Cathepsin K (CatK), a lysosomal cysteine protease predominantly expressed in osteoclasts, is an established target for anti-resorptive drug development. Here, an integrated computational workflow comprising virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, molecular mechanics/Poisson-Boltzmann surface area (MM/PBSA) calculations, and drug-likeness/ADMET prediction was used to prioritize natural product-derived CatK ligands from th
papers.summary: This study used an integrated computational pipeline—virtual screening, molecular docking, 300 ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations, and ADMET prediction—to identify natural product-derived compounds that inhibit cathepsin K, a key protease in bone resorption. The workflow prioritized candidate ligands with favorable binding stability and drug-like properties as potential anti-osteoporosis therapeutics. The findings are computational predictions requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Donor-Type-Dependent Heterogeneity of Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Lung Transplantation: A Multi-Cohort Transcriptomic Interaction Analysis of DCD Versus DBD Lungs.
papers.abstract: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) and donation after brain death (DBD) donor lungs are widely used in lung transplantation yet managed as equivalent with respect to ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI), despite fundamentally different ischemic backgrounds: warm ischemia in DCD versus neurogenic-inflammatory priming in DBD donors.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-cohort transcriptomic interaction analysis to show that ischemia-reperfusion injury in lung transplantation differs mechanistically between DCD and DBD donor lungs, reflecting distinct ischemic backgrounds (warm ischemia vs. neurogenic-inflammatory priming). The findings suggest DCD and DBD lungs should not be managed as equivalent with respect to IRI.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: SF-DTI is a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that addresses two key challenges: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein data modalities, and underuse of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. It combines multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement to improve DTI prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Quinazoline-tethered thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors: green synthesis, molecular docking, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-fused heterocycles have attracted considerable research interest in pharmaceutical, medicinal, organometallic, and materials chemistry. In this work, two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives were synthesized using choline hydroxide as an environmentally friendly catalyst. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT). Compound 11e showed the highest inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 0.599 µg mL-1 (1.305 µM). Molecular docking was performed to examine
papers.summary: This study reports the green synthesis of two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives using choline hydroxide as an eco-friendly catalyst. The compounds were tested against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase, with compound 11e showing the strongest inhibition (IC50 = 0.599 µg/mL). Molecular docking was used to explore how these compounds bind to the enzyme.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and preliminary anticancer evaluation of diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives: in vitro, in vivo and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of cancer-associated mortality and morbidity worldwide, and there is a continued need for structurally diverse anticancer agents with improved properties. The present study reports a series of diphenylpropan-1-one (DPP) derivatives (4a-4i), rationally designed around a chalcone framework and synthesized via a three-step reaction sequence. The physicochemical and spectral characterization of the synthesized derivatives was performed using spectral techniques. Their anticancer potential was evaluated through a preliminary in vitro cytotoxicity screening against t
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of nine diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives based on a chalcone scaffold, followed by preliminary anticancer testing. The compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity in vitro, with additional in vivo and in silico analyses, suggesting potential as breast cancer agents. The work is an early-stage medicinal chemistry effort identifying candidate compounds for further development.

papers.title: The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists.
papers.abstract: Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level "Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy." We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.
papers.summary: This perspective reviews how large language model-driven AI agents are moving drug discovery beyond static, task-specific tools toward autonomous 'virtual scientists.' The authors propose a 6-level 'Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy' to gauge system maturity and argue for evaluation paradigms based on full-chain traceability, while outlining adoption barriers and positioning agents as scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning framework for peptide lead optimization in ultralarge design spaces.
papers.abstract: In modern peptide drug discovery, the incorporation of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) has become a powerful strategy to improve potency and key developability properties, including stability, solubility, and oral bioavailability. This shift has expanded peptide chemical diversity and design spaces well beyond natural residues, creating fundamental challenges for predictive methods (e.g., quantitative structure-activity relationship modeling) used in lead optimization: limited transferability from natural residues to novel ncAAs, limited interpretability, and poor scalability to ultralarge pe
papers.summary: This paper presents an interpretable machine learning framework for optimizing peptide leads that incorporate noncanonical amino acids, addressing the challenge of navigating ultralarge chemical design spaces. The approach aims to improve transferability, interpretability, and scalability compared to traditional QSAR methods for peptide drug discovery.

papers.title: Large-scale prospective evaluation of co-folding across hundreds of Mac1-ligand complexes and three virtual screens.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Bo
papers.summary: This study prospectively evaluates deep-learning co-folding methods (including AlphaFold3) on 489 newly determined SARS-CoV-2 Mac1–ligand complex structures that were released after the models' training cutoffs, avoiding data leakage. It also assesses how well these methods perform in three virtual screening campaigns, testing both structure prediction and affinity ranking. The work provides a large, independent benchmark for co-folding in a drug-discovery context.

papers.title: Integrative pan-cancer analysis of AKT1 and structure-based drug design by buckwheat derived compounds.
papers.abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Sheikh et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. AKT1 is a serine-threonine protein-kinase involved in tumour cell proliferation, survival, metabolism, and therapeutic resistance via activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. However, the comprehensive pan-cancer characterization of AKT1 and systematics identifications of natural AKT1 inhibitors remains limited. T
papers.summary: This study performs a pan-cancer analysis of AKT1, a kinase central to the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway that drives tumor growth and therapy resistance, to characterize its expression and role across cancer types. The authors then use structure-based drug design to identify natural compounds derived from buckwheat as potential AKT1 inhibitors. The work combines large-scale cancer genomics with computational drug discovery to propose new natural-product leads targeting AKT1.

papers.title: Transforming the Landscape of Drug Innovation in AI Era: AlphaFold 3 and Beyond.
papers.abstract: The traditional drug discovery and development (DDD) pipeline has long been characterized by inefficiency and high costs. The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI), especially AI-based toolkits for protein structure and interaction prediction, exemplified by AlphaFold 3 (AF3), promises to reshape the landscape of drug innovation. AF3 advances structural biology by predicting protein structures and their interactions with a range of biomolecules, including nucleic acids, small-molecule ligands, and ions, potentially changing the conventional DDD paradigm, although prediction accuracy
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI-based protein structure and interaction prediction tools, particularly AlphaFold 3, are reshaping drug discovery and development. AF3 extends beyond protein structure prediction to model interactions with nucleic acids, small molecules, and ions, potentially transforming the traditional drug development pipeline. The authors also note limitations in prediction accuracy that remain to be addressed.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Brightfield Detection of Anti-Fibrotic Effects in a 3D Retinal Fibrosis Model.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) spheroid and microtissue models are increasingly used in phenotypic drug discovery, yet their scalability for high-throughput screening often remains limited, constrained by the cost and complexity of conventional imaging-based readouts. Here, we present a morphology-based screening approach using low-resolution brightfield images of human retinal pigment epithelium microtissues (hRPE-MTs) to identify fibrotic and non-fibrotic phenotypes. The results of this study demonstrate that extracting geometric, intensity, and texture features from segmented spheroids enables quan
papers.journal: SLAS discovery : advancing life sciences R & D
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning approach that uses low-resolution brightfield images of 3D human retinal pigment epithelium microtissues to distinguish fibrotic from non-fibrotic phenotypes. By extracting geometric, intensity, and texture features from segmented spheroids, the method enables scalable, cost-effective screening for anti-fibrotic compounds without expensive imaging readouts.

papers.title: TechBio 3.0 closes the drug discovery loop with multimodal AI and generative chemistry.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed molecular prediction and design, yet these advances remain only partially integrated with experimental discovery. We define TechBio 3.0 as an emerging paradigm for closed-loop drug discovery that connects multimodal molecular representations, generative chemistry, and automated experimentation. We examine its early preclinical and clinical evidence, identify remaining technical and translational barriers, and argue that this convergence is beginning to define biotechnology's next era.
papers.summary: This perspective article defines 'TechBio 3.0' as an emerging paradigm that closes the drug discovery loop by integrating multimodal molecular representations, generative chemistry, and automated experimentation. The authors review early preclinical and clinical evidence for this convergence, identify remaining technical and translational barriers, and argue it marks biotechnology's next era.

papers.title: Exploiting Neosartorya (Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2-defined fungal targets for drug repurposing against Candida albicans.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections caused by Candida albicans remain major clinical challenges because of the limited therapeutic options, toxicity, and emerging resistance. Drug repurposing offers a promising strategy to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging existing compounds with known safety profiles. In this study, we applied a structure-based drug repurposing approach guided by the antifungal protein Neosartorya (currently Aspergillus) fischeri antifungal protein 2 (NFAP2), which targets fungus-specific intracellular proteins, including glutamate decarboxylase, mitochondrial ATP synthase
papers.summary: This study uses the antifungal protein NFAP2 from Aspergillus fischeri as a guide to identify fungus-specific protein targets in Candida albicans, then applies structure-based drug repurposing to find existing compounds that hit those targets. The approach aims to accelerate antifungal discovery by leveraging drugs with known safety profiles against a pathogen with limited treatment options and rising resistance.

papers.title: Using structure to evaluate the accuracy and transferability of machine learning potentials of biomolecules.
papers.abstract: Molecular simulation is a powerful tool to describe chemical and physical processes across length scales. Fundamental tradeoffs between the accuracy of quantum mechanics and speed of classical models makes simulating biosystems very difficult. Machine learning potentials (MLPs) offer a potential solution which combines the accuracy of electronic structure theory with the computational scaling of classical approaches. Applying MLPs to biosystems could unlock new developments in drug discovery, biological mechanisms and interactions. Despite this promise, rigorous benchmarks are needed to determ
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks machine learning potentials (MLPs) for biomolecular simulation by using structural accuracy as a criterion, addressing the tradeoff between quantum accuracy and classical speed. It evaluates both the accuracy and transferability of MLPs across different biomolecular systems, providing needed rigor for applying MLPs to drug discovery and biological mechanisms.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mass Spectrometry-Based Metabolomics and Lipidomics for Drug Discovery and Development.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence applied to mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics has advanced through three technological generations: chemometric and classical machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with large language models so far entering mainly at the edges. The metabolome and lipidome lie closest to drug action, yet they have been among the slowest omics layers to adopt modern artificial intelligence. This paradox arises from their downstream position, which leaves them without a closed molecular reference and without the standardized, readily model
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of AI in mass spectrometry-based metabolomics and lipidomics across three generations: classical chemometrics/machine learning, deep learning, and self-supervised foundation models, with LLMs playing only a peripheral role so far. It argues that despite metabolomics and lipidomics being closest to drug action, they have lagged in AI adoption due to the lack of a closed molecular reference and standardized, model-ready data. The paper frames this paradox and likely outlines opportunities for AI-driven drug discovery and development in these omics layers.

papers.title: ProDTI: Prior-Guided Positive-Unlabeled Learning for Robust Drug-Target Interaction Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate Drug-Target Interaction (DTI) prediction is critical for drug discovery. While deep learning advances this field, the fundamental lack of verified negative interactions inevitably causes biased risk estimation. Although formulating DTI prediction as a Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning problem is theoretically sound, directly applying PU learning to deep models suffers from early-stage optimization instability and decision boundary ambiguity.
papers.summary: ProDTI introduces a prior-guided positive-unlabeled learning framework to address the lack of verified negative drug-target interactions, which biases deep learning DTI predictors. By incorporating prior knowledge to stabilize early optimization and clarify decision boundaries, the method aims to make PU-based DTI prediction more robust and reliable.

papers.title: GNPS-assisted identification of bioactive constituents from Scoparia dulcis and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms via network pharmacology and experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Scoparia dulcis L. (SD) is an edible medicinal herb traditionally consumed as a cooling beverage in tropical Asia for the management of metabolic and inflammatory disorders; however, its dietary bioactive constituents and anti-inflammatory mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. In the present study, the metabolite profile of the aerial parts of SD (ASD) was characterized, and their anti-inflammatory potential was evaluated through an integrated approach incorporating LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking, network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in v
papers.summary: This study used LC-HRMS/MS-based molecular networking (GNPS) to profile metabolites from Scoparia dulcis, an edible medicinal herb used traditionally for inflammatory disorders. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations were combined with experimental validation to identify bioactive constituents and their anti-inflammatory mechanisms. The work provides a framework for linking dietary plant metabolites to anti-inflammatory targets.

papers.title: Cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I from Salvia miltiorrhiza: integrated in vitro and computational evaluation of their antidiabetic potential.
papers.abstract: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (Lamiaceae) is a traditional medicinal plant rich in bioactive tanshinones with diverse pharmacological properties. However, comparative information regarding experimentally measured activity and computational interaction profiles of individual tanshinones remains limited. This study aimed to compare cryptotanshinone (1) and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I (2), isolated from S. miltiorrhiza, using an integrated in vitro and computational approach. The compounds were obtained through activity-informed phytochemical fractionation and evaluated for inhibition of α-glucosidase
papers.summary: This study isolated two tanshinone compounds from Salvia miltiorrhiza and compared their antidiabetic potential using both laboratory assays and computational modeling. Both cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I showed inhibitory activity against α-glucosidase, with computational docking supporting their binding interactions. The work provides comparative evidence for these natural compounds as potential antidiabetic agents.

papers.title: Integrated In silico and In Vitro Evaluation of Piperine Derivatives as Potential Efflux Pump Inhibitors in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antibiotic resistance mediated by efflux pump activity represents a major challenge in the treatment of infections caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Efflux pumps such as NorA and MepA reduce intracellular antibiotic accumulation and contribute significantly to decreased antibiotic efficacy. In this study, PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, was evaluated as a potential efflux pump inhibitor using an integrated in silico and in vitro approach. Computational analysis, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, Lipinski r
papers.summary: This study evaluates PBSA-7, a piperine-derived compound, as a potential efflux pump inhibitor against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Using molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and in vitro assays, the authors show that PBSA-7 interacts with efflux pumps NorA and MepA, which are responsible for reducing antibiotic efficacy. The findings suggest piperine derivatives could serve as adjuvants to restore antibiotic sensitivity in resistant bacterial strains.

papers.title: Thymol-based derivatives as anticancer agents: design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies.
papers.abstract: Seventeen thymol-based derivatives (TM1-7, TBr1-2, TCl1-4, and TF1-4) were designed and synthesized by esterification with halo- and non-halogenated cinnamoyl molecules employing a key-step coupling reaction. All derivatives were chemically characterized (1H NMR, 13C NMR, HR-MS, and HPLC analysis) and evaluated for their potential anticancer properties. The anti-proliferative effectiveness was assessed using an MTT assay against four cancer cell lines (U87MG, SHSY-5Y, MDA-MB-231, and JIMT1) and human dermal fibroblasts (HDFa) compared to Triton X-100. Among the thymol-based derivatives, TM7 an
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized seventeen thymol-based derivatives by esterifying thymol with various cinnamoyl molecules, then tested their anticancer activity against four cancer cell lines and normal fibroblasts. The most promising compound, TM7, showed notable anti-proliferative effects, and molecular docking studies were used to explore its potential binding interactions with cancer-related targets.

papers.title: Discovery and biological characterization of 1-[4-(2-difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU): A novel thiazolyl-urea chemotype targeting yellow fever virus and host casein kinase 2 (CK2).
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a re- emerging mosquito- borne flavivirus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high case- fatality rates. Due to vaccine contraindications, incomplete immunization coverage, and the absence of approved specific antivirals, host- directed drug discovery targeting cellular machinery exploited by YFV is a critical therapeutic priority. Here, 1-[4-(2- difluoromethoxyphenyl)- 5- methylthiazol- 2- yl]- 3-(naphthalen- 1- yl)urea (DFMNTU) was synthesized, characterized by NMR, MS, and HPLC, and evaluated for antiviral efficacy against YFV strain 17 D in Vero cells. DFM
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of DFMNTU, a novel thiazolyl-urea compound that targets yellow fever virus by inhibiting the host protein casein kinase 2 (CK2). The compound showed antiviral activity against YFV strain 17D in Vero cells, suggesting host-directed antiviral strategies may be viable for flavivirus treatment.

papers.title: Design-Evolution Synergy Enables New-to-Nature Enzyme Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution and machine-learning-assisted evolution have transformed biocatalysis by enabling rapid optimisation of catalytic performance within compatible protein scaffolds. In parallel, advances in deep-learning-driven de novo protein design have expanded accessible protein architectural space, enabling the generation of functional catalysts for increasingly challenging transformations. We herein report a synergistic design-evolution strategy to encode new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination reactions using engineered de novo haemproteins to synthesise chiral piperidin
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports a hybrid strategy that combines deep-learning-based de novo protein design with directed evolution to create engineered haemoproteins capable of new-to-nature regio- and enantioselective C-H amination. The approach expands the accessible protein scaffold space and then optimizes catalytic performance, enabling synthesis of chiral piperidine products. It demonstrates that design and evolution can be synergistically combined to access reactions not found in nature.

papers.title: Identification of YES1 Inhibitors From Approved Drugs Using a Multimodal Deep Learning Framework.
papers.abstract: While anti-human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) drugs, including trastuzumab improve the prognosis of patients with HER2-positive cancers, acquired resistance by cancer cells remains a significant clinical challenge. We had previously reported that YES1 is overexpressed in trastuzumab-resistant breast and lung cancer cells, and that its inhibition restores trastuzumab sensitivity. However, no approved drug specifically targets YES1. In this study, as a drug repositioning approach aimed at rapid clinical application, we constructed a machine learning model capable of learning the int
papers.summary: The authors built a multimodal deep learning framework to identify approved drugs that could inhibit YES1, a kinase implicated in trastuzumab resistance in HER2-positive breast and lung cancers. Since no approved drug specifically targets YES1, this drug-repositioning approach aims to find existing drugs that could restore trastuzumab sensitivity and be rapidly repurposed clinically.

papers.title: Novel Flavonoid Senotherapeutics Identified by Phenotypic Drug Discovery Reduce Senescence and Improve Multiple Markers of Healthspan.
papers.abstract: Senescent cells are a key driver of aging and contribute to many age-related diseases. Senolytics, agents that selectively eliminate senescent cells, offer a promising therapeutic strategy to treat age-related diseases but face significant barriers to clinical translation. Fisetin, a natural flavonoid senolytic, has progressed to clinical trials but is limited by suboptimal efficacy and poor bioavailability. To address these challenges, we developed two novel fisetin-derived flavonoid senolytics, SR29384 and SR31133, using an integrative phenotypic drug discovery approach. These compounds exhi
papers.summary: Researchers used phenotypic drug discovery to develop two new fisetin-derived flavonoid senolytics, SR29384 and SR31133, that overcome the poor efficacy and bioavailability of the natural compound fisetin. These novel compounds reduce senescence and improve multiple markers of healthspan, offering a more translationally viable strategy for targeting senescent cells in age-related diseases.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is a promising anticancer target, and the integrated computational approach was used to prioritize candidate compounds from marine sources.

papers.title: A multiparametric in vitro strategy for small molecule drug-induced liver injury risk mitigation in early drug development.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) remains a major cause of preclinical and clinical attrition, reflecting persistent gaps in the predictive translation of preclinical safety data to human outcomes. To address these gaps, we established a refined multiparametric framework for early DILI risk prediction using a balanced reference set of 170 drugs with established clinical outcomes. Thirty physicochemical, mechanistic endpoints, and exposure-related features were systematically evaluated to identify high-specificity predictors of intrinsic DILI risk. Cytotoxicity in primary human hepatocytes and h
papers.journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology
papers.summary: This study develops a multiparametric in vitro framework for predicting drug-induced liver injury (DILI) risk using a balanced set of 170 drugs with known clinical outcomes. By evaluating 30 physicochemical, mechanistic, and exposure-related endpoints, the authors identify high-specificity predictors, including cytotoxicity in primary human hepatocytes, to improve early-stage safety assessment. The approach aims to reduce late-stage attrition by better translating preclinical data to human DILI risk.

papers.title: Targeting a Leukemia-Relevant Protein-Protein Interface: N-Aryl Anthranilic Acids as Disruptors of the c-Myb-CBP/p300 KIX Interaction.
papers.abstract: The interaction between c-Myb and the CBP/p300 KIX domain is a key transcriptional event in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and represents an attractive target for small-molecule intervention. In this study, we applied an integrated computational-experimental strategy to identify new N-aryl anthranilic acid disruptors of the c-Myb-KIX protein-protein interaction. A scaffold-focused library of 3656 N-aryl anthranilic acid derivatives was filtered, docked to the c-Myb-binding groove of KIX (PDB 2AGH), and the top hits were further evaluated by MD simulations, MM/PBSA, FEL, and ADMET analyses. This
papers.summary: This study uses computational screening (docking, MD simulations, MM/PBSA, ADMET) of a 3656-compound N-aryl anthranilic acid library to identify new small molecules that disrupt the c-Myb–CBP/p300 KIX protein-protein interaction, a key transcriptional event in acute myeloid leukemia. The work nominates candidate compounds for further experimental validation as potential AML therapeutics.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Cotula cinerea Essential Oil: Integrated Chemical, In Vivo, Histological, and Computational Evaluation.
papers.abstract: The anti-inflammatory activity of Cotula cinerea essential oil (EO) was evaluated using integrated chemical, in vivo, histological, and computational approaches. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) identified trans-thujone (51.86%), santolina triene (10.60%), and sabinene (6.17%) as the most abundant constituents. In benzylthiouracil (BTU)-treated Wistar rats, EO administration reduced the liver and kidney indices from 4.36% to 2.70% and from 0.65% to 0.52%, respectively; red blood cell count increased from 4.90 to 7.17 × 1012/L and hemoglobin from 9.40 to 15.40 g/dL. Aspartate aminot
papers.summary: This study evaluates the anti-inflammatory properties of Cotula cinerea essential oil using chemical profiling (GC-MS), in vivo rat experiments, histological analysis, and computational modeling. The oil's major components (trans-thujone, santolina triene, sabinene) were associated with reduced liver and kidney indices and improved hematological parameters in treated rats. The integrated approach suggests potential therapeutic anti-inflammatory applications, though the abstract is truncated.

papers.title: Synthesis and Cytotoxic Activity of 1,3-Selenazole-2-Amine Derivatives With Computational ADMET Profiling.
papers.abstract: A set of newly developed 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives (1-4) was prepared via a modified Hantzsch-type cyclization of appropriately substituted α-bromoacetophenones with selenourea under reflux conditions. The synthesized compounds were tested for cytotoxic activity in HT-29 (colon cancer), MCF-7 (breast cancer), and L929 (mouse fibroblast) cell lines using the MTT assay. The compounds induced weak to moderate cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells. Among them, compound 4 showed cytotoxic activity with IC50 value of 171.10 µM, while no appreciable activity was observed against HT-29 cells (IC50 > 30
papers.summary: This study synthesized four new 1,3-selenazole-2-amine derivatives via a modified Hantzsch-type cyclization and tested their cytotoxicity against colon cancer (HT-29), breast cancer (MCF-7), and normal mouse fibroblast (L929) cell lines. The compounds showed only weak to moderate activity, with the best compound (4) having an IC50 of 171.10 µM against MCF-7 and essentially no activity against HT-29. Computational ADMET profiling was also performed to assess drug-likeness.

papers.title: Exploring the Neuropharmacological Potential of Ligustrum sinense Relevant to Parkinson's Disease: In Vivo and In Silico Study.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are valuable sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in neurodegenerative disorders. This study investigated the antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities of Ligustrum sinense (L. sinense) leaf extract through in vitro, in vivo, and in silico approaches. Antioxidant activity assessed by the DPPH assay demonstrated moderate free radical scavenging capacity (IC50 = 73.56 ± 2.18 µg/mL) compared with l-ascorbic acid (IC50 = 7.29 ± 2.86 µg/mL). Behavioral evaluations using the open field, hole cross, elevated plus maze,
papers.summary: This study evaluates leaf extracts of the medicinal plant Ligustrum sinense for antioxidant, neuropharmacological, and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitory activities using in vitro, in vivo (rodent behavioral tests), and in silico (molecular docking) approaches, with relevance to Parkinson's disease. The extract showed moderate antioxidant activity and behavioral effects suggestive of neuropharmacological potential, though it was weaker than the positive control l-ascorbic acid.

papers.title: Selective PTP1B inhibition by A-1331852: Uncompetitive kinetics and computational evidence for C-terminal engagement.
papers.abstract: Selective inhibition of protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B (PTP1B), a well-established target in metabolic and oncological signaling pathways, is limited by its 74% active-site identity with the closely related phosphatase TCPTP. Repurposing the clinical-stage Bcl-xL BH3 mimetic A-1331852, we identify it as a potent PTP1B inhibitor demonstrating a selectivity margin of at least 50-fold over TCPTP (IC₅₀ = 4.0 μM vs >200 μM). Kinetic analysis reveals uncompetitive inhibition consistent with recognition of a substrate-induced binding site. Docking and 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations (MD) of fu
papers.summary: The clinical-stage Bcl-xL inhibitor A-1331852 was found to selectively inhibit the phosphatase PTP1B with at least 50-fold selectivity over the closely related TCPTP. Kinetic analysis indicates uncompetitive inhibition, suggesting it binds a substrate-induced site rather than the active site, and docking plus 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations support engagement of the C-terminal region. This offers a potential scaffold for developing selective PTP1B inhibitors that avoid cross-reactivity with TCPTP.

papers.title: Enzymatic N-deacylation is the predicted membrane-disruption switch for sphingomyelin: a falsifiable in-silico framework for sphingolipid vulnerability in ALS.
papers.abstract: Sphingolipid dysregulation is an emerging feature of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), but no systematic method separates species that may worsen axon-myelin membrane integrity from matter that may counteract it. We present an in-silico framework classifying sphingolipids and designed derivatives as candidate membrane-disruptive or candidate protective species, scored against real biological referents using externally published tools rather than a bespoke composite. Its central finding concerns a single, chemically defined difference in lipid state. In coarse-grained (MARTINI 3) molecular d
papers.summary: This paper presents an in-silico framework that classifies sphingolipids and designed derivatives as either membrane-disruptive or protective, using published tools rather than a custom scoring system. The central claim is that enzymatic N-deacylation acts as a predicted membrane-disruption switch for sphingomyelin, offering a falsifiable hypothesis about sphingolipid vulnerability in ALS. The work is computational and hypothesis-generating rather than experimentally validated.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and genome mining strategies for activating cryptic polyketide biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces: an overview.
papers.abstract: Beneficial microbes from soil or marine habitats are promising sources for discovery of new bioactive compounds for medicine and agriculture, largely through biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) that encode the production of complex natural products for drug and antibiotic discovery. However, most BGCs are transcriptionally silent under standard testing conditions and may require a complex, integrated approach for activation. In this review, we revisit previous approaches to activating BGCs, focusing on polyketides. We additionally discuss how integrating genome mining strategies with multi-omics
papers.summary: This review surveys strategies for activating silent polyketide biosynthetic gene clusters in Streptomyces, a major source of bioactive natural products for drug and antibiotic discovery. It highlights how combining genome mining with multi-omics approaches can overcome the transcriptional silencing that typically hides these clusters under standard laboratory conditions.

papers.title: Lab to codes: multimodel advanced AI-driven pipelines to drive antimicrobial peptide design for the post-antibiotic era.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of global antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has outpaced the development of new antimicrobial agents, necessitating transformative approaches such as AI-driven in-silico drug discovery. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are promising alternatives due to their broad-spectrum bactericidal activity and limited susceptibility to resistance. However, the transition from bench to bedside remains constrained by certain challenges, such as instability, potency, and cytotoxicity. Here, well-integrated, multi-model AI-driven pipeline strategies for the mining and discovery of novel AMPs are
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This review discusses how integrated multi-model AI pipelines can accelerate the discovery and design of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights how AI can address key bottlenecks such as peptide instability, potency, and cytotoxicity that hinder clinical translation. The paper outlines strategies for mining and engineering novel AMPs in silico.

papers.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A co
papers.summary: MolecureAI is an autonomous AI agent platform for closed-loop drug discovery that uses cost-ordered cascade evaluation to enforce chemical correctness via structural invariants rather than relying on model capability. It addresses four unresolved capability gaps: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop.

papers.title: A review of advances in research on mechanisms inhibiting kidney stone formation from a network pharmacology perspective.
papers.abstract: Nephrolithiasis is a prevalent, highly recurrent urological disorder affecting 1%-15% of the global population, with 5-year recurrence rates reaching up to 50%. While surgical interventions achieve acute stone clearance, they do not resolve underlying metabolic derangements, crystal-induced tubular injury, or chronic inflammatory cascades. Natural products from global ethnomedicinal systems (including Traditional Chinese Medicine, Indian Ayurveda, Persian Unani medicine, European phytotherapy, and African ethnopharmacology) demonstrate potent multi-target anti-urolithic properties. However, de
papers.summary: This review examines how natural products from various ethnomedicinal traditions may inhibit kidney stone formation, using a network pharmacology framework to understand their multi-target mechanisms. It highlights that while surgery removes stones acutely, it doesn't address underlying metabolic and inflammatory processes, and natural compounds show promise as multi-target anti-urolithic agents.

papers.title: Knowledge graph and machine learning-guided virtual screening prioritizes putative blockers of the PSMD11/Rpn6-EBOV glycoprotein interface.
papers.abstract: Host-directed antiviral discovery requires a traceable route from host-factor identification to testable molecular hypotheses. This study developed such a workflow around a host factor associated with Ebola virus glycoprotein (EBOV GP).
papers.summary: This study presents a workflow that combines knowledge graph analysis with machine learning-guided virtual screening to identify potential small-molecule blockers of the interaction between the host protein PSMD11/Rpn6 and the Ebola virus glycoprotein. The approach provides a traceable path from host-factor identification to testable molecular hypotheses for host-directed antiviral discovery.

papers.title: Commentary: Identification of diagnostic genes for myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury associated with metabolic syndrome through the integration of bioinformatics analysis, molecular docking and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This commentary discusses a study that used bioinformatics integration, molecular docking, and experimental validation to identify diagnostic genes linking myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury with metabolic syndrome. It highlights the study's approach to uncovering shared molecular mechanisms and potential biomarkers for these interconnected conditions.

papers.title: Single‑Cell in silico Perturbation Uncovers a Ferroptosis Regulatory Network for Cigarette Smoke‑Induced Skin Aging and Identifies Dapivirine as a Candidate Agent.
papers.abstract: Cigarette smoke exposure induces cutaneous ferroptosis and accelerates skin aging, yet the core regulatory genes and targeted interventions remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key ferroptosis-driving genes underlying smoke-induced skin senescence, clarify their mechanisms, and screen candidate small molecules that reverse smoke-related skin damage.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell in silico perturbation to identify a ferroptosis regulatory network driving cigarette smoke-induced skin aging, pinpointing key ferroptosis-related genes involved in this process. The authors then screen small molecules and identify dapivirine as a candidate agent that can reverse smoke-related skin damage. The work links ferroptosis biology to skin senescence and proposes a repurposed drug for potential intervention.

papers.title: Integrated counter current separation and omics approaches for discovery of bioactive compounds from medicinal plants.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants provide an important source of structurally varied bioactive metabolites with medicinal potential; however, their effective extraction, characterization, and standardization present considerable analytical challenges. Counter-current separation (CCS) methods, such as centrifugal partition chromatography (CPC) and high-speed counter-current chromatography (HSCCC), represent advanced liquid-liquid chromatographic approaches that minimize irreversible adsorption of samples. A systematic literature search was performed in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Sci
papers.summary: This review examines how counter-current separation (CCS) techniques like CPC and HSCCC can be integrated with omics approaches to discover and characterize bioactive compounds from medicinal plants. The authors argue that combining these liquid-liquid chromatographic methods with metabolomics and related omics tools improves extraction, identification, and standardization of plant-derived bioactive metabolites.

papers.title: Multimodal profiling uncovers an aging-associated ETS1-MYO1B vascular niche responsive to ipragliflozin.
papers.abstract: Tissue aging involves complex changes in vascular, immune, and stromal compartments that collectively reshape the local tissue ecosystem and may contribute to age-related diseases, including cancer, fibrotic diseases, and cardiovascular disease. However, it remains unclear whether reproducible, cell-specific vascular niche states emerge during aging and whether these states can be therapeutically targeted.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: Using multimodal profiling, the authors identify a reproducible aging-associated vascular niche state defined by ETS1-MYO1B expression that emerges across tissues during aging. This niche can be therapeutically modulated by ipragliflozin, suggesting a druggable target for age-related vascular dysfunction.

papers.title: Lightweight 2D-Convolutional Neural Network for Drug-Kinase Binding Affinity Prediction with Minimal Encoded Representations.
papers.abstract: Drug-kinase binding affinity (DKBA) prediction plays a crucial role in prioritizing compounds and reducing the time and financial resources required for drug discovery. However, many existing deep learning models rely on complex molecular representations, such as molecular graphs or pretrained embeddings, which may increase computational complexity and limit scalability.
papers.journal: Iranian journal of pharmaceutical research : IJPR
papers.summary: This paper introduces a lightweight 2D-convolutional neural network for predicting drug-kinase binding affinity using minimal encoded molecular representations, avoiding complex graph-based or pretrained embeddings. The approach aims to reduce computational complexity and improve scalability while maintaining predictive performance for compound prioritization in drug discovery.

papers.title: Advances in deep learning for antimicrobial research.
papers.abstract: The rapid spread of antimicrobial resistance and the lag in the development of new antimicrobial drugs have become major challenges for global public health. Conventional methods for discovering antimicrobial drugs are characterized by long development cycles and high costs, which are further exacerbated by the rapid evolution of bacterial resistance. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop efficient computational methods to accelerate the identification of drug resistance mechanisms and the research and development process of new antimicrobial drugs. In recent years, the new generation
papers.summary: This review discusses how deep learning methods are being applied to antimicrobial research, particularly to combat antimicrobial resistance and accelerate drug discovery. It highlights the need for computational approaches to overcome the slow, costly traditional pipelines for identifying resistance mechanisms and developing new antimicrobial drugs.

papers.title: AI-guided ethnopharmacology for cardiovascular drug discovery: from biomedical data to experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Despite substantial advances in pharmacological therapy, cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Botanical drugs represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites, yet their translation into modern cardiovascular therapeutics remains limited by chemical complexity, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and challenges in experimental validation. Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of biomedical data resources and advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have created new opportunities to systematically investigate botanical drugs beyond empirical a
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence can be integrated with ethnopharmacology to accelerate the discovery of cardiovascular drugs from botanical sources. It outlines a workflow that moves from mining biomedical data resources through AI-driven prediction to experimental validation, addressing challenges like chemical complexity and incomplete mechanistic understanding of plant-derived compounds.

papers.title: A survey on ethical digital twins in healthcare.
papers.abstract: Digital Twins for Health (DT4H), defined as dynamic, data-driven, in silico representations of individuals, organs, medical devices, clinical workflows, or healthcare systems, are emerging as a promising paradigm for transforming healthcare. DT4H systems have the potential to advance personalized medicine, treatment optimization, disease prediction, drug discovery, clinical trials, and health system planning. However, their real-world development and deployment also raise important ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI). Because DT4H systems rely on sensitive longitudinal health data a
papers.summary: This survey examines the ethical, legal, and social implications (ELSI) of Digital Twins for Health (DT4H), which are dynamic, data-driven virtual representations of individuals, organs, devices, or healthcare systems. It highlights how these systems could advance personalized medicine, drug discovery, and health system planning, while also raising concerns around sensitive longitudinal health data and real-world deployment. The paper aims to map these ethical challenges to guide responsible development of DT4H technologies.

papers.title: Placental alkaline phosphatase promotes lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy and represents a potential target for statin repurposing.
papers.abstract: Lumbar spinal stenosis is a prevalent degenerative disorder driven primarily by ligamentum flavum hypertrophy. Emerging evidence links ectopic lipid accumulation to fibrotic remodeling and suggests a potential contribution of immune dysregulation. However, the molecular targets connecting lipid accumulation with ligamentum flavum fibrosis remain incompletely defined. We sought to evaluate the underlying mechanisms of lipid-lowering drug targets in lipid-associated ligamentum flavum fibrosis.
papers.summary: This study identifies placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP) as a driver of lipid accumulation and fibrosis in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, a key cause of lumbar spinal stenosis. The authors propose that statins, already used for lipid lowering, could be repurposed to target this pathway and slow disease progression.

papers.title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore ana
papers.summary: This study used a 3D convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder combined with LSTM-based molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived drug candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors for restless legs syndrome. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened via pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, and pharmacophore analysis. The work demonstrates an AI-driven de novo design pipeline for dopaminergic compounds, though experimental validation is not reported.

papers.title: Identification of flavonoids from natural products against hyperlipidaemia through computational approaches.
papers.abstract: Over the centuries, hyperlipidaemia has been recognised as a major risk factor contributing to cardiovascular disease (CVD). Current research increasingly explores natural compounds such as flavonoids for their potential lipid-lowering effects. This study evaluated pharmacological potential of flavonoids to identify strong inhibitors for target receptor, Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type (PCSK9). A total of 29 compounds, including one FDA-approved drugs were screened for drug-likeness and ADMET properties, followed by molecular docking and Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations using PC
papers.summary: This study used computational approaches—drug-likeness and ADMET screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations—to evaluate 29 flavonoids (plus one FDA-approved drug) as potential inhibitors of PCSK9, a key target for lowering cholesterol. The work identifies candidate flavonoids with favorable pharmacological profiles that could serve as starting points for developing natural-product-based treatments for hyperlipidaemia.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.abstract: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a five-year survival rate of approximately 20-25% despite advances in targeted therapy and immunotherapy. There is a continuous need for novel, low-toxicity compounds capable of modulating key oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Mangrove ecosystems are rich reservoirs of bioactive phytochemicals, yet the inhibitory potential of compounds from Rhizophora mucronata against validated lung cancer-associated proteins has not been systematically explored using multi-scale computational approaches.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and simulation methods to screen phytochemicals from the mangrove plant Rhizophora mucronata as potential inhibitors of proteins linked to lung cancer. The authors identify candidate compounds that may modulate oncogenic pathways in non-small cell lung cancer, though findings remain purely in silico and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Preclinical identification of an oxadiazole-pyrazole lead targeting prostate cancer through integrated mechanistic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among men, while resistance to androgen deprivation therapy emphasizes the need for new therapeutic strategies. Molecular hybridization of pharmacologically relevant heterocycles offers a rational approach for developing novel anticancer agents.
papers.summary: This study identifies and preclinically evaluates an oxadiazole-pyrazole hybrid compound as a potential lead for prostate cancer therapy, motivated by resistance to androgen deprivation therapy. The work uses integrated mechanistic evaluation to characterize the compound's anticancer activity, though the abstract provides only the rationale rather than specific results.

papers.title: Mechanism-aware and safety-validated AI for drug repurposing: a critical review and translational pharmacology framework.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted drug repurposing seeks to identify new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Nevertheless, most of the existing studies are centered on prediction scores and candidate ranking, and there is still relatively little attention paid to the pharmacological mechanisms, safety and translational validation.
papers.summary: This critical review argues that AI-driven drug repurposing has been overly focused on prediction scores and candidate ranking while neglecting pharmacological mechanism validation, safety assessment, and translational readiness. The authors propose a translational pharmacology framework that integrates mechanism-awareness and safety validation into AI repurposing pipelines.

papers.title: Identification of natural TLR4 modulators through network pharmacology and molecular modeling in SARS-CoV-2 Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection.
papers.abstract: Viral-bacterial co-infection with SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii exacerbates hyperinflammation via Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated immune pathways. Using network pharmacology, an integrated protein-protein interaction network identified 30 key inter-species hubs comprising viral, bacterial, and human host proteins, with TLR4 achieving a high MCC score (722), highlighting its high topological centrality as a host immune target. Virtual screen of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex identified three top candidates, CID5898023, CID5403474, and CID74977829, with docki
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to identify TLR4 as a central host immune hub in SARS-CoV-2 and Acinetobacter baumannii co-infection, based on its high topological centrality in an integrated protein-protein interaction network. Virtual screening of 2,820 natural compounds against the TLR4/MD-2 complex yielded three top candidate modulators (CID5898023, CID5403474, CID74977829) with favorable docking scores. The work proposes natural compounds as potential anti-inflammatory agents targeting TLR4-driven hyperinflammation in co-infection.

papers.title: Therapeutic Antitoxoplasmosis Potential of Garcinia cambogia: Evidence From In Silico and In Vivo Studies.
papers.abstract: Toxoplasma gondii, an opportunistic protozoan, is widely prevalent and poses potential health risks. Its treatment remains challenging with several side effects, urging the exploration of new, safe, and efficient drugs. We aimed to explore the therapeutic efficacy of the medicinal plant Garcinia cambogia (GC) against both acute and chronic toxoplasmosis. Sixty Swiss albino mice were allocated into five groups: I (healthy), II (model), III (spiramycin [SPM] treated, IV (GC treated), and V (SPM + GC treated). Each group is further divided into two subgroups receiving treatment at 4 and 42 days p
papers.summary: This study evaluated Garcinia cambogia extract as a treatment for Toxoplasma gondii infection using both computational (in silico) predictions and mouse experiments. The plant extract showed therapeutic effects against acute and chronic toxoplasmosis, with the combination of Garcinia cambogia and the standard drug spiramycin appearing most effective. The findings suggest Garcinia cambogia could be a safe, plant-based adjunct or alternative for treating toxoplasmosis.
